preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless postalveolar fricative [ʃ] to the glottal fricative [h]: the oral constriction is lost and only glottal friction remains. In Finnic, Proto-Uralic *š became h after South Estonian had split off, so Proto-Uralic *šiŋere 'mouse' gives Finnish hiiri, against Hungarian egér and Erzya чеерь.

examples.note: Finnic *š > h came after South Estonian had split off; compare Hungarian egér.
Compare Erzya чапамо, Meadow Mari шопо.

sources: Sammallahti, P. (1988). Historical phonology of the Uralic languages. In D. Sinor (Ed.), The Uralic Languages: Description, History and Foreign Influences (pp. 478–554). Brill. https://doi.org/10.1163/9789004492493_021
